Meeting Header: Date: 2026-06-03 10:00 PDT | Duration: 62 minutes | Attendees: Nicole Carter, Arjun Patel, Maya Li, Samir Das, Elena Ruiz, James O'Neill, Alex Kim

[00:00] Nicole: Okay, hi everyone. Thanks for joining. We'll get started in a sec. Uh, mic check — can you hear me?
[00:05] Multiple: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:09] Nicole: Great. Welcome to the June all-hands. Quick agenda — business update, product & engineering highlights, hiring and people, then open Q&A.
[00:18] Nicole: First off, big thanks — Q2 bookings are pacing ahead of plan, we closed a few Dedicated deals and a Private pilot with a major regulated customer, so shout out to sales and solutions. Not going to drop numbers in public channels yet but team leads will get the deck after.
[00:32] Arjun: I'll take the product/eng infra bits. On latency and cost — we've seen a 12% reduction in median token latency for small models after the recent kernel swap, and cost-per-token for our most common workload is down about 8% from March. There are some outliers — long-seq retrieval-heavy workloads still spike.
[00:48] Arjun: We're shipping a KV cache metrics dashboard next week, so operators can see prefix hit rates, cold start counts, and effective batching. Note, the telemetry labels may show up as K V cash in some logs — small thing we're fixing.
[01:02] Maya: Quick follow up — the runtime patch also has a fallback for a rare OOM on 40B sequences; it's been validated on the canary pool. Please run any internal perf tests against the canary image before approvals.
[01:15] Speaker 1: Sorry, can I ask a clarification — the canary pool, is that dedicated capacity only or also in hosted?
[01:20] Maya: Good question — it's in Dedicated first, but we roll the same image to hosted canaries later in the week.
[01:25] Samir: On product — Dedicated autoscale is moving to beta next week. The default policy will try to keep median latency under the SLA target while optimizing for unit cost; there are presets for latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive workloads. We want teams to use the presets as starting points.
[01:40] Samir: Also we're releasing a new quantization recommendation guide — it's not a silver bullet, but for typical chat workloads the 2.3 quant profile gives 25-35% cost reductions with minimal quality regression on our eval sets. Elena's team will publish the eval artifacts.
[01:55] Elena: Yep, the evals are up — note that some prompts show a small hallucination uptick in the extreme edge cases; we'll mark those prompts as regression risk and share mitigations. "quantizashun" in transcribe — sometimes the captioning spelled it weird in the draft slides, so ignore that.
[02:08] Nicole: Security and compliance — James?
[02:10] James: We're expanding SOC 2 scope to include parts of Private; the external audit firm will start scoping work in July. Also rolling out mandatory refresher on SSO and new RBAC templates next week. For customers asking about KMS/HSM integration, ops has the current doc in the security repo and we'll be sharing an executive summary with customers on request.
[02:26] James: Reminder — please don't paste production credentials in public threads. We've had a couple of near-misses.
[02:31] Audience chuckle / nervous glances
[02:34] Nicole: Hiring — James O'Neill: we are still hiring aggressively in infra, SRE, and sales-engineering. We will add 10 headcount this quarter across those buckets. Managers, please accelerate referrals and prioritize final rounds for candidates already in loop.
[02:49] James O'Neill: We're also piloting a new interview rubric for IC3+ to reduce bias and speed decisions; more in the recruiting channel.
[02:56] [03:00] Alex: Quick marketing & go-to-market note — PLG motion continues to perform, but enterprise motion is picking up — expect more product marketing assets for Dedicated & Private this month. We'll push a one-pager for security FAQs for sales to use.
[03:12] Audience question: How are we thinking about price vs performance positioning vs competitors?
[03:16] Nicole: We position on predictable inference economics more than raw price; we bake in predictable latency and fallback behavior. Competitors mentioned in threads are OpenAI and Anthropic — we watch their feature launches but our play is reliability + cost controls + private deployment options.
[03:30] [03:35] Arjun: Ops note — some customers asked for on-prem packaging; engineering has a simplified installer path in progress but the real blocker is support and test harnesses. We're building test infra to validate air-gapped installs.
[03:49] [03:55] Maya: Regarding telemetry, please tag any customer-facing experiments with feature flags and include a short description in the experiment tracking sheet; we had a mis-synced experiment that created confusion last month.
[04:05] [04:10] Audience: Can you comment on the Dedicated SLA — any penalties if we miss latency?
[04:13] Samir: We're still finalizing exact SLA language with legal, but the target SLA will include credits for availability; latency SLOs will be operationally backed with fallback policies. We'll share the proposed SLA in the next product update.
[04:27] Nicole: Quick customer stories — closed a pilot with a fintech customer using Private with strict data residency. They liked our KV cache behavior and deterministic fallbacks. Also a gaming studio is testing Dedicated for scale spikes.
[04:45] [04:50] Elena: Research update — we've landed two attention optimizations that shave off about 7% runtime cost for long-context workloads; will appear in next week's runtime image. There's also a prototype for mixed-precision training-to-inference path but it's early.
[05:03] [05:08] Nicole: Ok open Q&A — remember to drop questions in chat, and we'll address common ones in follow-up notes.
[05:14] Audience Q: Any org changes?
[05:16] Nicole: No large-scale reorganizations planned. We are moving two hires to report to infra instead of platform to speed iteration. Names and managers will be communicated by People Ops after today's meeting.
[05:29] Audience Q: Are we re-prioritizing roadmap items because of the Private pilot?
[05:33] Samir: A bit — we fast-tracked audit logging and KMS integrations for the pilot; other items are still on schedule.
[05:40] [05:45] Nicole: Last minute things — please fill the all-hands survey, it helps shape the next format. Thank you to the ops folks who fixed last week's incident quickly.
[05:56] Maya: One more operational note — when filing incidents please include the canary image tag and the exact model version; it saves us an hour or two.
[06:08] Nicole: Alright, that's it. Slides and recording will be posted. Action owners please follow up. Thanks everyone.
[06:17] Meeting ended.

Notes: Transcript is auto-generated and contains imperfect transcription (occasional mis-hearings and spacing). References to internal repos, decks and experiment sheets were made — these are shared in #all-hands and the company drive.
